slot.brief: Ask which radical species initiates ozone decomposition in the stratosphere and identify the catalytic chain steps; include one statement about CFCs vs NOx.

stem: Which option identifies the radical released by CFC photolysis, its ozone-depletion cycle, and the role of $\text{NO}_x$ correctly?
options: CFC photolysis releases $\dot{\text{Cl}}$; $\dot{\text{Cl}}+\text{O}_3\rightarrow\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}+\text{O}_2$, then $\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}+\text{O}_2\rightarrow\dot{\text{Cl}}+\text{O}_3$; $\text{NO}$ is regenerated in a separate catalytic cycle.

CFC photolysis releases $\dot{\text{Cl}}$; $\dot{\text{Cl}}+\text{O}_3\rightarrow\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}+\text{O}_2$, then $\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}+\text{O}\rightarrow\dot{\text{Cl}}+\text{O}_2$; $\text{NO}$ is regenerated in a separate catalytic cycle.

CFC photolysis releases $\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}$; $\dot{\text{Cl}}+\text{O}_3\rightarrow\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}+\text{O}_2$, then $\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}+\text{O}\rightarrow\dot{\text{Cl}}+\text{O}_2$; $\text{NO}$ is regenerated in a separate catalytic cycle.

CFC photolysis releases $\dot{\text{Cl}}$; $\dot{\text{Cl}}+\text{O}_3\rightarrow\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}+\text{O}_2$, then $\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}+\text{O}\rightarrow\dot{\text{Cl}}+\text{O}_2$; unlike chlorine radicals, $\text{NO}$ is consumed stoichiometrically and is not regenerated from $\text{NO}_2$.

verdicts.working: CFC photolysis releases Cl·. The sequence Cl· + O₃ → ClO· + O₂, then ClO· + O → Cl· + O₂ regenerates chlorine; NO is also regenerated in its separate catalytic cycle.

working:
CFC photolysis releases $\dot{\text{Cl}}$.
$\dot{\text{Cl}}+\text{O}_3\rightarrow\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}+\text{O}_2$
$\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}+\text{O}\rightarrow\dot{\text{Cl}}+\text{O}_2$
$\text{NO}+\text{O}_3\rightarrow\text{NO}_2+\text{O}_2$
$\text{NO}_2+\text{O}\rightarrow\text{NO}+\text{O}_2$

Independent check: CFC photolysis releases Cl·. The sequence Cl· + O₃ → ClO· + O₂, then ClO· + O → Cl· + O₂ regenerates chlorine; NO is also regenerated in its separate catalytic cycle.
solution:
CFC photolysis releases $\dot{Cl}$, which is regenerated in the catalytic cycle:
$$\dot{Cl}+O_3\rightarrow Cl\dot{O}+O_2,\qquad Cl\dot{O}+O\rightarrow\dot{Cl}+O_2$$
Similarly, $NO$ is regenerated in the separate cycle $NO+O_3\rightarrow NO_2+O_2$ and $NO_2+O\rightarrow NO+O_2$. Thus, option (B).
